name: Ratio de Compresión de Texto
description: Utiliza data compression algorithms para medir text redundancy and predictability as indicators of AI generation.
useCase: Detección de texto generado por IA through lower information density and higher compressibility
mechanism: Compresses the input text using lossless algorithms (gzip, zlib, LZ77) and computes the ratio de compresión (compressed size / original size). generado por IA text typically compresses more efficiently due to higher regularity, more repetitive patrones, and lower information entropía compared to texto humano. The method also analiza the ratio de compresión of sliding windows para detectar segments with varying compressibility—a sign of mixed human/AI authorship.
source: Jiang, Z. et al. (2024) - Detecting LLM-Generated Text in Computing Education: A Comparative Study for ChatGPT Cases, IEEE Access
algorithm: Multi-Algorithm Compression + Ratio Analysis + Sliding Window Segmentation
parameters: Algorithms: gzip-9/zlib/brotli, Window: 200-500 chars sliding, Metrics: global ratio, segment ratios, ratio varianza, Min text: 200 words
strengths:
• No se requieren datos de entrenamiento (unsupervised)
• Language and model agnostic
• Extremely fast computation
• Captures information-theoretic properties
limitations:
• Lower precisión on short texts
• Technical text with repeated terms compresses well naturally
• Depends on compression algorithm choice
• Not sensitive to semantic-level patrones

references.title: Jiang, Z. et al. (2024). Detecting LLM-Generated Text in Computing Education. IEEE Access.
Benedetto, D. et al. (2002). Language Trees and Zipping. Physical Review Letters.
Mireshghallah, F. et al. (2024). Smaller Language Models are Better Black-box Machine-Generated Text Detectors. EACL.
